title: Human authority is explicit and machine authority is derived without elevation
statement: Every human-principal mutation performed through DEVAI MUST identify exactly one caller-declarable constitutional role through an invocation flag or explicit valid authority-session reference and MUST ignore ambient role/session state for authorization; a derived machine contract MUST declare its non-empty allowed initiator-role set, runtime MUST bind exactly one actual role from that set matching the invocation/declaration, and derivation MUST preserve and MUST NOT erase, substitute for, widen, or elevate that initiator or consent; the bootstrap identity MAY plan or orchestrate but MUST NOT authorize mutation, and cross-role bootstrap apply batches MUST use distinct invocation/declaration boundaries, each using either a direct flag or valid authority session.
rationale: Articles 6-10 make role declaration and separation load-bearing. An implicit role or caller-selected machine actor would turn the authority boundary into advisory metadata.

strategy.rationale: The registered test corpus provides deterministic regression evidence for this invariant.
